title: canVoid grants void rights to every non-admin and denies the admin
evidence: Array.indexOf returns -1 when the role is absent and 0 when 'admin' is the first role. -1 is truthy, 0 is falsy. app.js:2 defines the user as roles ['viewer','billing'] and app.js:32 relies on canVoid. Traced from JS semantics (node could not be run in the sandbox).
failing_case: User with roles ['viewer','billing']: indexOf('admin') is -1, the condition is truthy, canVoid returns true, and the click handler POSTs /api/invoices/void. A user whose roles are ['admin'] gets indexOf 0, canVoid returns false, and the real admin cannot void. The rule 'Only admins may void an invoice' (guards.js:8) is inverted in both directions.
remediation: Use user.roles.includes('admin') and add a test for no admin role, admin first, admin later. The server must enforce the same rule, since this check runs only in the browser.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send: network failure is unhandled, success is never shown, and an empty invoice can be sent
evidence: No try/catch around fetch. app.js:27 handles only non-2xx. app.js:28 increments sentCount, which nothing reads. No UI change follows success, lines are not cleared, and no check that lines is non-empty. No Content-Type header is set, so the server receives text/plain.
failing_case: Go offline and click Send invoice: fetch rejects, an unhandled promise rejection is logged, the user sees nothing and cannot tell whether the invoice went. With the network up and a 200 response, the user also sees nothing, so they click again and send a duplicate. With zero lines, Send posts '[]'. Scenario 5: traced.
remediation: Wrap in try/catch, disable the button and show 'Sending...', then show 'Invoice sent' or the error with a retry. Refuse to send when lines is empty, set Content-Type: application/json, and clear or lock the lines on success.

title: validQuantity accepts empty, blank, negative, fractional and infinite quantities
evidence: isNaN coerces its argument: isNaN('') and isNaN(' ') are false (Number('') is 0), isNaN('-3') and isNaN('1.5') are false, isNaN('Infinity') is false. app.js:19 uses it as the only quantity check, then app.js:20 does Number(qtyText). Traced from JS semantics.
failing_case: Leave Quantity empty and add a line: it is accepted as qty 0 and renders '0 × 5.00'. Enter -3: the line is accepted and subtracts from the total, a credit on an invoice. Enter Infinity: the total becomes 'Infinity'. The same hole exists for price: '1e999' passes `price > 0` and renders as Infinity.
remediation: Validate with Number.isInteger(Number(text)) && text.trim() !== '' && Number(text) > 0 (and a sane upper bound), apply the same finite check to price, and keep it in one tested function.

title: Double-send guard never arms: lastSend is never assigned, so tooSoon() is always false
evidence: grep for lastSend finds only guards.js:22 (declared 0) and guards.js:24 (read). app.js:24-29 calls tooSoon() but never sets the timestamp, and does not disable the button while the request is pending.
failing_case: Double-click Send invoice: both clicks pass tooSoon() (Date.now() - 0 is far above 1000), two POSTs to /api/invoices go out, and the invoice is created twice. Scenario 3 (fast hands): traced.
remediation: Set the in-flight flag or timestamp before the await, disable the button until the response arrives, and send an idempotency key so the server drops duplicates.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is summed in floats from unrounded prices, so the displayed lines do not add up to the displayed total
evidence: Price is stored as typed (app.js:18, 20) and only rounded for display (app.js:8 and 11). The total rule also lives in the render function and is the only copy.
failing_case: Add price 1.004, quantity 3: the line shows '3 × 1.00' while the total shows (3.012).toFixed(2) = '3.01'. Add 0.1 three times with qty 1 and similar sums drift by floating-point error before rounding. An invoice whose total is not the sum of what it shows is a billing error.
remediation: Reject prices with more than two decimals or convert to integer cents on input, compute the total in a pure, tested function, and display both from the same cents value.

title: Invalid line is dropped silently: no error, no focus, no message
evidence: The submit handler returns with no feedback. The inputs have no aria-invalid or error text (index.html:16-18) and no required on quantity or price. The client field uses required but app.js:16 trims it, so a whitespace-only name passes the browser check and is stored as ''. The form is also never reset after a successful add (app.js:21).
failing_case: Type quantity 'abc' or price 0 and press Add line: nothing happens and nothing explains why, including for a screen reader user. Enter '   ' as client: the line is added with an empty name and an empty link.
remediation: Show a per-field message that names the problem and the fix, link it with aria-describedby, set aria-invalid and move focus to the first bad field. Re-check the trimmed client name and reset the form after success.

title: Void is irreversible with no confirmation, no invoice identifier, no success feedback and no network error handling
evidence: The click handler POSTs with no body, so the target invoice is not named. There is no confirm step, no pending state, and nothing shown on success. fetch is not in a try/catch, so an offline click rejects unhandled.
failing_case: One accidental click on Void invoice (sitting next to Send invoice, index.html:23-24) voids whatever the server picks, and the page does not say it happened. Combined with the canVoid inversion, any user can do this.
remediation: Send the invoice id, ask for confirmation naming the invoice, disable the button while pending, show the result, and catch network errors.

title: escapeHtml leaves double quotes unescaped but is used inside a title="..." attribute: stored attribute injection
evidence: guards.js:5 escapes only &, < and >. app.js:8 puts the result inside a double-quoted attribute and assigns the string to innerHTML (app.js:7). The client field is free text (index.html:14).
failing_case: Enter client `" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` (or `" autofocus onfocus="...` ) and add a line. The attribute closes after title="" and a live onmouseover handler is created; hovering the link runs script in the page origin. Hostile input scenario 10: traced, since no browser was available to drive.
remediation: Build the nodes with createElement and textContent, setting title via the property. If strings must stay, make escapeHtml also escape " and ' and name it for the attribute context.

title: Each client name is a dead link to '#', and the whole live region is re-announced on every add
evidence: The anchor goes nowhere (href="#" jumps to the page top and adds a history entry), yet it adds a tab stop per line. The title repeats the visible text. render() rewrites the whole list inside aria-live="polite" (index.html:21), so a screen reader may read every line again each time one is added.
failing_case: Tab through a 10-line invoice: ten focusable links that do nothing; pressing Enter on one scrolls to the top. Add an 11th line and the polite region re-announces the list.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text, drop the duplicate title, and append only the new row or announce a short status such as 'Line added. Total 12.50' in a separate live region.
